explain.say: Look at the arrow. Iron is higher in the reactivity series than copper, so it loses electrons more easily. Iron atoms give electrons to the copper ions in the solution. Who do you think ends up as the metal?

explain.say: Copper! See the nail? A pink-brown coat of copper metal forms on it. The iron has pushed the copper out of its compound. We say iron displaces copper, which means it takes its place. Have you seen that colour on a copper coin?

explain.say: Now look at the solution. The blue fades towards pale green, because iron sulfate forms instead of copper sulfate. Iron plus copper sulfate gives iron sulfate plus copper. Do you think copper could push iron out of iron sulfate?

faq.a: A displacement reaction is when a more reactive metal pushes a less reactive metal out of its compound. Iron plus copper sulfate gives iron sulfate plus copper.
Iron is higher in the reactivity series, so it gives up electrons more easily than copper. The copper ions take those electrons and become copper metal.
asks: Why does the nail turn copper coloured?

faq.q: Why does the blue colour fade?
faq.a: The blue comes from copper ions in solution. As they turn into copper metal there are fewer of them, and the iron ions that replace them give a pale green colour.
asks: Why does copper sulfate lose its colour?

faq.a: Aluminium powder reacts with iron oxide, displacing the iron. It gives out so much heat that the iron comes out molten, which is used to weld railway tracks.

faq.q: How can displacement reactions show the reactivity series?
faq.a: Try each metal in solutions of the others. A metal that displaces many others is high in the series; one that displaces none is low.

facts: Iron + copper sulfate → iron sulfate + copper; iron displaces copper because iron is more reactive.
The thermite reaction between aluminium and iron oxide produces molten iron at temperatures above 2,000 °C.
